welcome_arch.title: Welcome to Rexon
welcome_arch.description: Rexon is a desktop environment manager for Linux. Install it to use it like any other application:
benefits: Rexon appears in the application menu, together with an emergency item for restoring the desktop appearance.
Live wallpapers work in GNOME and Cinnamon too.

modes.title: For everyone on this computer
modes.description: Rexon will appear in the application menu for everyone who uses this computer. The administrator password is needed once. Missing components are installed along the way, and Rexon will ask for the password less often when changing the system.

modes.title: Just for you
modes.description: Rexon will appear in the application menu for you only. No password is needed, but this option does not install missing components either.

welcome_arch.dontAskAgainHint: This window will not appear again. Rexon will keep running from the folder it is in.

consent.title: Don't ask for the password for Rexon actions
consent.checkbox: Allow Rexon to change the system without a password
consent.description: Normally Rexon asks for the administrator password before changing the system. With this permission on, Rexon actions will not ask for the password. The permission is off by default.
consent.what: What is allowed: only installing desktop environments from Rexon's list. Login and boot screen themes and installing or removing other software still ask for the password.
consent.who: Who: members of the administrators group, and only while they are sitting at this computer. Remote logins are asked for the password as usual.
consent.risk: The risk: any program running under your account will be able to install desktop environments from Rexon's list through Rexon (and turn on their login screen if the system has none) without your confirmation.
consent.undo: How to undo: uninstall Rexon from its menu (☰ → “🗑️ Uninstall Rexon”) — the permission is removed together with the application.
consent.hint:
Permission file: /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-rexon-nopasswd.rules
Administrators group: wheel (Debian and Ubuntu use their own administrators group)

de_reason_astra_zps.title: Astra Linux SE security blocks the installation
de_reason_astra_zps.problem: Astra Linux Special Edition runs a closed software environment: it only starts software signed by the vendor. Desktop environment packages carry no such signature, so the installation cannot succeed — it would fail somewhere in the middle.
de_reason_astra_zps.advice: What you can do: turn the closed software environment off (administrator rights and a reboot are required) — or install the desktop on Astra Linux CE, which has no such restriction.
de_reason_astra_zps.explanation:
Astra Linux Special Edition runs a closed software environment: it only starts software signed by the vendor. Desktop environment packages carry no such signature, so the installation cannot succeed — it would fail somewhere in the middle.

What you can do: turn the closed software environment off (administrator rights and a reboot are required) — or install the desktop on Astra Linux CE, which has no such restriction.

de_reason_astra_no_repos.title: This desktop is not in the Astra Linux repositories
de_reason_astra_no_repos.problem: The stock Astra Linux package sources only carry its own Fly desktop. There are no “gnome” packages there, so there is nothing to download.
de_reason_astra_no_repos.advice: What you can do: add the Debian package sources — Astra is based on Debian, and the required packages will show up afterwards.
de_reason_astra_no_repos.explanation:
The stock Astra Linux package sources only carry its own Fly desktop. There are no “gnome” packages there, so there is nothing to download.

What you can do: add the Debian package sources — Astra is based on Debian, and the required packages will show up afterwards.

de_reason_osnova_closed.title: OSnova repositories are not public
de_reason_osnova_closed.problem: OSnova is a certified distribution with closed package sources. There is no public place to download desktop environments from, so Rexon has nothing to fetch.
de_reason_osnova_closed.advice: What you can do: request the package source from your system vendor (it usually comes with the licence) and add it — Rexon will see the desktops afterwards.
de_reason_osnova_closed.explanation:

de_reason_alt_unsupported_de.title: ALT Linux: this desktop is not supported yet
de_reason_alt_unsupported_de.problem: ALT Linux builds its own packages under its own names. The mapping for “cosmic” is not described yet, so Rexon does not know what to install.
de_reason_alt_unsupported_de.advice: What you can do: pick one of the desktops verified on ALT Linux — kde, gnome, xfce, mate, cinnamon-mint, budgie, hyprland, lxqt.

de_reason_cosmic_unavailable.title: COSMIC is not packaged for this distribution yet
de_reason_cosmic_unavailable.problem: COSMIC is a young desktop and is not packaged everywhere yet. This distribution's package sources do not carry it.

de_reason_rosa_no_task_package.title: ROSA Linux: installation is possible, but not guaranteed
de_reason_rosa_no_task_package.problem: ROSA installs desktops through its own task-* package sets, and there is none for “budgie”. Rexon will try the regular Fedora groups, but ROSA's package sources may not have them.
de_reason_rosa_no_task_package.advice: You may continue: if the packages are missing, the installation simply stops and nothing breaks. Installed without a warning: kde, gnome, xfce, mate, lxqt.

de_reason_steamos_not_yet.title: SteamOS: this desktop environment can't be installed yet
de_reason_steamos_not_yet.problem: On SteamOS Rexon builds a desktop as a system extension from Valve's own package sources, and so far only Xfce, LXQt, Hyprland have been checked this way. This desktop hasn't been checked yet: it may need parts that SteamOS keeps for itself (login screen, drivers), so Rexon doesn't offer it.
de_reason_steamos_not_yet.advice: Xfce, LXQt and Hyprland can be installed on SteamOS: Rexon builds them as system extensions and rebuilds them by itself after every system update.
